Priya —

Thanks — glad to see the NDA in place. High-level we can support an ephemeral, embargoed exchange. Sketching a MAP below (short form):

1) Provisioning (Day 0–2): Redwood creates ephemeral S3 bucket + short-lived credentials (7-day TTL). We will not snapshot or index the dataset.
2) Sandbox run (Day 3–10): Redwood runs perf/latency sweeps and safety checks against your prompt pack in an isolated project.
3) Acceptance (Day 11–14): Luma verifies results; sign-off triggers either extended sandbox or takedown.
4) Takedown (Day 15): Automated deletion of all copies from Redwood systems; you get a deletion report.

Required constraints we need to formalize in the MAP: no training/fine-tuning on raw data, no export of raw files, only aggregated metrics leave the sandbox, logs retained for 30 days for debugging and then purged (we can provide audit logs).

Can Monica and Neha help with the specific security wording and whether 7-day tokens are feasible from infra side?

If this looks good we’ll draft a short MAP doc and a DocuSign envelope for the exchange authorization.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Partner Integrations

Sergio —

Agree with the sketch. Proposed security wording to include verbatim in the MAP: 

- Provisioning: Redwood will provide a single-use, time-limited S3 access token (7-day TTL). Token rotation is automatic; any extension requires written approval from Luma legal and Redwood security.
- Local copies: Authorized Redwood engineers may create ephemeral local copies only for debugging; local copies must be deleted within 7 days and owners must submit a signed deletion attestation.
- Logging/audit: Redwood will persist request/response logs (metadata and derived metrics) for 30 days for debugging. Raw payloads will be redacted and never used for training; upon takedown Redwood will produce a signed deletion report listing S3 object keys removed and logs purged.
- No training: Data will not be used to fine-tune or evaluate models outside the isolated sandbox without explicit written consent.

Operational timeline (recommended):
- Day 0–2: Token provisioning and preflight checks
- Day 3–9: Performance & safety runs (7 days)
- Day 10–11: Customer review and acceptance
- Day 12: Automated takedown and delivery of deletion manifest

I’ll draft the short MAP and the deletion template; Neha, can you confirm the automated deletion report format and whether we can sign programmatically for the manifest (e.g., PDF with checksum)?

—Monica
